subject: toucan
reasoning:
I'm designing a stylized toucan module with the SDK—working out proportions like overall length, bill size, and standing height, then planning the skeleton starting with a hip root for the joint rig.

From there I'm building the spine chain as a curved path from tail to chest, then continuing with a neck chain running forward and upward from the spine's tip toward the head base, assigning names and roles to each joint along the way.

I define the head joint aimed forward-up, then add a separate jaw joint parented to the head for the lower mandible, positioned slightly forward and down using local offsets. For the bill, I'm planning a swept shape along a curved path from the head forward, tapering the radius toward the tip and banding colors to capture the classic toucan look—yellow/orange base transitioning to a black tip.

I'm settling on color bands for the bill—yellow near the base, orange mid, black at the tip—and planning the lower mandible as a shorter sweep from the jaw joint using similar tapered bezier geometry. For the eyes, I'm working out how to position a ring of blue skin around the head using local coordinate offsets for the toucan's characteristic eye patch.

Now I'm figuring out how to sweep the body as a rounded black-feathered form along the spine chain, using radius profiles to get that classic toucan chest shape.

Working out the leg geometry now, with hip sockets positioned relative to the body radius and feet planted on the floor plane, plus a tapered black tail chain hanging off the hips with a backward-bending knee for the perched bird pose.

With the sole mode, bends need one fewer direction since the sole fixes the joint above the final segment, so I'll use just one bend vector for the three-segment setup. I'm working out reach distances to make sure the thigh, shin, and foot lengths roughly match the target position without stretching unnaturally. I'll go with the sole-based approach and build the chain with four joint names (hip, knee, ankle, toe) mapped to the four path points.

Now I'm figuring out the toucan's zygodactyl toes -- two forward, two back -- attached at the foot tip using small capsule shapes angled outward from the toe end point, keeping the geometry simple rather than sweeping a full bezier curve.

Now I'm working out small folded wings on the body's sides, using an extruded outline attached at a point along the spine chain via its tangent frame, with the wing shape defined in a forward/up plane for a tucked, angled profile.

Next I'm adding a dark blue eye ring using a small sphere primitive positioned at the head.

For colors, I'm sticking with a limited palette (black, cream, orange, yellow, red, blue, green) to keep things simple -- black head, cream chest, orange-yellow bill with banded colors transitioning toward the tip, and red accents under the tail using sector painting. The head itself I'm building as a sphere primitive attached to the head bone.

For the neck and chest, I'm thinking about whether to add a bright bib patch or just keep the black neck flowing into the cream belly sectors on the body. Feet will get a dark grey tone, and I'm skipping decal-based eyes for now, focusing instead on the sweep-based tail chain parented to the spine.

Now I'm defining the color palette and starting the main build function, setting up the hips joint and spine chain using a catmull curve with keyframe positions for the toucan's torso.

I'm continuing to lay out the skeleton—adding the tail chain curving down and back from the base of the spine, matching its taper radius to the body, then adding the neck chain branching off the spine's upper joint, carefully checking how joint indices map to the spine's span positions.

Now I'm placing the head joint off the neck's end, then the jaw joint angled forward from the head. I'm also working through the sweep geometry for the upper bill, defining its curve with bezier points relative to the head and tapering radius with color bands for yellow, orange, and black sections.

Still writing bill geometry...

Now I'm defining the lower bill as a similar sweep attached to the jaw, then placing the eyes as small spheres offset from the head with pupils to follow.

Still writing part placements...

Still defining leg chains and toe structure...

Realizing the overall scale is way too large for a real toucan -- body-to-bill proportions suggest I need to rescale everything down by roughly half, so I'm recomputing coordinates for the spine, tail, neck, head, bill, legs, and wings to hit a realistic ~0.58m total length with proper proportions between the chunky bill, compact body, and short perching legs.

I'm finalizing placement details for eyes, toe rods, wing outline geometry, and color sectors (cream belly, red tail underside), then writing the complete code with correct chain/sweep/rod signatures and returning the root bone.
